name: Electricity, low voltage, Czech grid mix (life-cycle incl. upstream and grid losses)
ecoinvent_proxy: market for electricity, low voltage | electricity, low voltage | CZ
notes: Direct generation intensity 0.45 kg CO2/kWh (Ember 2023) scaled by 1.22 for upstream fuel chains and T&D losses (ratio observed for DE between Ember direct 0.371 and ÖKOBAUDAT life-cycle 0.486). Other EF categories are filled from the ÖKOBAUDAT DE-2023 dataset scaled by the GWP ratio (approximation).

name: Urea (46-0-0), EU average production, excluding CO2 captured in product
ecoinvent_proxy: market for urea | urea | RER
notes: Fertilizers Europe regional reference values (DNV GL validated). 0.733 kg CO2/kg is captured in the product and released on hydrolysis (modelled explicitly). ADP-fossil ≈ 26 MJ/kg (0.58 kg NH3/kg × ~35 MJ + process energy; cf. 30.54 MJ/kg for urea in ecoinvent v2.2 cited by Porter et al. 2021).

name: Calcium chloride, industrial/technical grade (Solvay process by-product)
ecoinvent_proxy: market for calcium chloride | calcium chloride | RER
notes: ecoinvent v2.2 value reported by Porter et al. (2021); Deng et al. (2021) report 2.79 t CO2/t for HCl+limestone route in China (upper bound); allyl-chloride hypochlorination by-product route is lower (~0.3).

name: Calcium lactate pentahydrate (lactic acid neutralised with limestone, crystallised and dried)
ecoinvent_proxy: lactic acid production | lactic acid | RER (0.584 kg) + limestone (0.325 kg) + drying
notes: Stoichiometric estimate: 0.584 kg lactic acid (1.3 kg CO2e/kg fossil-only, Corbion sugarcane LCA −0.224 incl. biogenic uptake) + 0.325 kg CaCO3 (0.03) + 0.143 kg geogenic CO2 released on neutralisation + ~1 MJ/kg crystallisation/drying (0.07). Biogenic C content 0.234 kg C/kg handled by the chemistry module.

name: Lactic acid (88 %), fermentation of sugar, fossil-only footprint
ecoinvent_proxy: lactic acid production | lactic acid | RER
notes: Corbion/TotalEnergies Corbion: −0.224 kg CO2e/kg incl. biogenic uptake (1.47 kg CO2/kg) → ≈1.25 fossil-only; bagasse-based process up to 4.6 (literature).
